citations.name: habeas:coverage
citations.commentary:
Formatting requires a value of the uninhabited UnreadContents type.
 This empty match has no executable case; storage tests deliberately
 supply no content values and reject node reads at the domain boundary.

rationale: The `habeas:coverage` citation on `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/storage.rs#impl[UnreadContents/NodeContents]/fn[format]` is appropriate. The function has a body, so a function-level exception is allowed. The body is `match *self {}` on `enum UnreadContents {}`, which is uninhabited, so it can never run. The commentary gives a substantive reason, not just difficulty. It says formatting needs a value of an uninhabited type, so the empty match has no executable case. That matches the source. It also says the storage tests supply no content values and reject node reads at the domain boundary. That matches `impl[StoredGraph/Domain]/fn[node_content]` in the same file, which panics with "storage operations must not read graph contents" and returns the `UnreadContents` type. The explanation is in fenced citation commentary, as the built-in requires. The item has no other citations, so there is no redundant `{impl}` or `{test}` reference.
